coverage.note: Ten source-qualified reports, with earlier-source dates labeled catch-up and reported corporate plans and research distinguished from releases. Three technology and three term proposals remain deferred for canonical catalog and license/alias review; arXiv export metadata was inaccessible and coverage is not comprehensive.

tldr: llama.cpp's versioned C libraries, IBM's structured LLMON previews and new research on verifiability and distillation point toward more reliable, adaptable small-model systems, but benchmark and defense claims remain unreplicated.

Robotics simulation tooling is improving while the Federal Reserve highlights financial exposure around the AI infrastructure buildout; corporate plans, market risks and policy discussions are not treated as realized outcomes.

news.title: llama.cpp and ggml publish v1.0.0 with stricter library versioning
news.summary: The ggml-org team tagged llama.cpp v1.0.0, documenting public C API/ABI versioning and introducing FP8 KV caches, an MoE host-memory expert cache, new model support, audio speech serving, and server hardening.
news.why_it_matters: Library compatibility promises and optional memory-saving inference paths matter to local model deployers.
news.caveat: The release removes deprecated API interfaces. Memory/performance outcomes depend on model, backend and hardware; hardening changes do not prove comprehensive security.

news.title: IBM introduces LLMON-structured Granite 4.1 preview models
news.summary: IBM released experimental Granite 4.1 3B and 8B previews trained on LLM Object Notation, a token-delimited structure that explicitly binds instructions to data and requirements.
news.why_it_matters: Structured prompts could reduce confusion between agent instructions and untrusted retrieved or tool data while remaining practical for compact models.
news.caveat: Prompt-injection resistance and benchmark parity are author-reported, based on controlled tests; a learned boundary is not an enforcement guarantee, and IBM labels the previews non-production.

news.title: NVIDIA demonstrates validated SimReady assets in an Isaac Sim pick-and-place task
news.summary: NVIDIA published a reproducible workflow combining a robot arm, gripper and object assets with defined joint, mass and collision properties for a virtual pick-and-place example in Isaac Sim.
news.why_it_matters: Reusable simulation-aware assets can shorten initial robotics scenario setup and make failures in kinematics and contacts easier to diagnose.
news.caveat: This is a tutorial and assembled simulation demo, not a newly released robot or verified real-world autonomous deployment; asset licenses and simulator requirements differ.

news.title: Federal Reserve report puts AI first among surveyed financial-stability concerns
news.summary: In the November Financial Stability Report, AI-related risks were cited by 87% of 23 market contacts, up from 50% in the prior survey; the Fed also documents rapidly expanding financing for data centers and advanced computing.
news.why_it_matters: The findings connect compute infrastructure investment to systemic credit and market vulnerabilities, an important constraint on AI scaling.
news.caveat: These percentages describe a small survey of market contacts, not the Federal Reserve Board's own ranking of risks or a prediction that a crisis will occur. The report notes information generally through October 28.

news.title: Research proposes negative-only RL when a verifier can reliably reject but not confirm answers
news.summary: A November 12 arXiv preprint formalizes one-sided verifiability and proposes Negative-Only Policy Optimization, which suppresses verified bad outputs without positively rewarding merely unrefuted ones.
news.why_it_matters: The idea addresses training settings where unit tests or weaker critics produce trustworthy failures but misleading passes.
news.caveat: Reported improvements are paper-author results under selected tasks and verifiers, not independent replication or a universal improvement over conventional RL.

news.title: New theoretical study separates distillation's optimization gains from generalization claims
news.summary: An arXiv preprint analyzes generalized linear models and rank-one matrix approximation, arguing that knowledge distillation can speed optimization without necessarily improving generalization.
news.why_it_matters: A clearer mechanism may help SLM researchers decide whether teacher labels improve learning dynamics or final task accuracy.
news.caveat: The proofs apply to specific simplified model classes, and reported real-data experiments do not establish the same mechanism for frontier-scale Transformers.

news.title: Reuters describes Amazon's draft World Product Graph effort for AI shopping
news.summary: Reuters reviewed internal planning material for a possible Amazon World Product Graph intended to consolidate product attributes for search and AI-driven shopping amid competition from other agents.
news.why_it_matters: High-quality product knowledge bases could become a strategic bottleneck for reliable commerce agents and retrieval systems.
news.caveat: This is reporting about an internal draft, NOT a launched product. Amazon said the document was outdated and may not reflect current plans; the project may change or be canceled.

news.title: ElevenLabs previews an enterprise voice-notes and dictation assistant
news.summary: TechCrunch reports that ElevenLabs launched an early-access ElevenAI preview at its November 11 event, combining meeting notes, cross-meeting recall, dictation and agent-driven follow-up actions.
news.why_it_matters: The product demonstrates the convergence of speech recognition, organizational memory and action-taking assistants.
news.caveat: The November 11 event date differs from the November 13 report. The preview requires early-access signup; 90-plus-language and quality statements are provider claims, and recording raises consent/privacy questions.

news.title: EU leaders convene for AI competitiveness and governance talks
news.summary: Reuters reports EU leaders meeting in Dublin to debate AI investment, regulation and safety while financing disputes constrain proposed gigafactories.
news.why_it_matters: The meeting illustrates how compute access, industrial policy and model governance are becoming linked issues.
news.caveat: This source covers the meeting and agenda, not a finalized EU law, funded gigafactory program or independently established summit outcome.

news.title: Reuters identifies restricted-NVIDIA-chip reliance in more than $3 billion of Chinese AI projects
news.summary: A Reuters examination of more than 150 records found over $3.2 billion of Chinese AI-computing projects tied to restricted NVIDIA processors, spanning proposals, contracts and some installations.
news.why_it_matters: The findings show how chip restrictions, procurement uncertainty and infrastructure financing interact across the global compute supply chain.
news.caveat: The value includes infrastructure beyond chips, and projects are at different stages. Reuters did not establish how chips were obtained or connect the projects to separate allegations involving NVIDIA executives.
